config.title: List Rendering with map()

intro.title: List Rendering with map()
intro.body: In this lesson, you will learn how to render lists of data in React using the map() function. This is a fundamental skill for displaying dynamic content, such as todo items, product lists, or user comments. You'll practice transforming an array of data into a list of React elements, assigning unique key props for efficient updates, and handling edge cases like empty lists.
intro.usecase: List rendering is everywhere in modern web apps. You'll find it in social media feeds (posts, comments), e-commerce sites (product listings, search results), dashboards (notifications, activity logs), and any interface that displays collections of similar items. Mastering this pattern will enable you to create data-driven UIs that update automatically when the underlying data changes.

objectives: Render a list of items using the map() function
Assign unique key props to list items for React's reconciliation process
Handle empty lists gracefully with conditional rendering
Transform array data into JSX elements using map()
Understand the importance of key props for performance and correctness
Destructure object properties in map() callbacks for cleaner code

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, making React and useState available for use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the TodoList component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named TodoList that returns JSX. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns some JSX content, like a div with a heading.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the TodoList component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A TodoList component is defined and ready to be used.
successCriteria: A functional component named TodoList is defined and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the TodoList component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named TodoList and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check that it's named TodoList and returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize todos state with TypeScript
steps.instruction: Inside your TodoList component, initialize a state variable named 'todos' using useState, typed as an array of objects with id (number) and text (string) properties. Set the initial value to an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to provide the type annotation for the state variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TodoList component will have a typed state variable 'todos' initialized to an empty array, ready to store todo items.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call with type annotation for an array of objects with id (number) and text (string) properties, storing the state in a variable named 'todos'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the correct type annotation for an array of todo objects.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Use useState with the proper type annotation for an array of todo objects.

steps.title: Define Todo type interface
steps.instruction: Above your TodoList component, define a TypeScript interface named Todo with id (number) and text (string) properties.
steps.hint: Use the interface keyword to define the shape of a todo object.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Todo interface is defined, providing type safety for todo objects throughout the component.
successCriteria: An interface named Todo is defined with id (number) and text (string) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined an interface, but make sure it's named Todo and has the correct properties with their types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Todo interface isn't defined correctly. Create an interface named Todo with id (number) and text (string) properties.

steps.title: Add sample todos to state
steps.instruction: Inside your TodoList component, add a useEffect hook that sets the todos state to an array of 3 sample todo objects when the component mounts. Use the setTodos function.
steps.hint: Import useEffect from react, then use it to update state when the component mounts. Each todo should have a unique id and descriptive text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will populate the todos state with sample data when it first renders, providing content to work with during development.
successCriteria: A useEffect hook is added that calls setTodos with an array of at least 3 todo objects, each with unique ids and text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added useEffect, but make sure it sets todos to an array of at least 3 sample todo objects with unique ids.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useEffect hook is missing or incorrect. Add useEffect that sets todos to an array of sample todo objects when the component mounts.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: In the TodoList component's return statement, replace 'null' with a div container that will hold the todo list UI.
steps.hint: Return a JSX div element as the root container for your todo list interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TodoList component now returns a div container instead of null, providing a structure to hold the todo list elements.
successCriteria: The TodoList component returns a JSX div element
The return statement no longer returns null
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element from the TodoList component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TodoList component should return a div container instead of null.

steps.title: Render the todos list using map()
steps.instruction: Inside your TodoList component's return statement, use the map() function to render the todos array as a list of div elements. Each div should display the todo text and have a unique key prop set to the todo id.
steps.hint: Use curly braces to embed the map() call in your JSX. For each todo, return a div with the text and a key prop.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will display each todo's text in its own div element, with the list updating automatically when the todos state changes.
successCriteria: The return statement includes a map() call on the todos array, rendering each todo's text in a div with a key prop set to the todo's id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using map() on the todos array, returning a div for each todo with the text and a key prop set to the id.
steps.feedbackWrong: The todos list isn't rendered correctly. Use map() to create a div for each todo, displaying its text and setting the key prop to its id.

steps.title: Add empty state message
steps.instruction: Modify your TodoList component to display a 'No todos yet!' message when the todos array is empty, using a ternary operator for conditional rendering.
steps.hint: Use the ternary operator to check todos.length. If 0, render the message; otherwise, render the mapped list.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a 'No todos yet!' message when the todos array is empty, providing better user feedback.
successCriteria: The return statement uses a ternary operator to check if todos is empty, rendering a message if true and the mapped list if false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added conditional rendering, but make sure it checks todos.length and displays 'No todos yet!' when empty.
steps.feedbackWrong: The empty state isn't handled correctly. Use a ternary operator to show 'No todos yet!' when todos.length is 0.

steps.title: Define addTodo handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your TodoList component, define a function named addTodo that takes a text parameter and adds a new todo to the todos state. The new todo should have a unique id (you can use the current length of the array + 1) and the provided text.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setTodos with a new array containing the existing todos plus the new todo object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The addTodo function will allow new todos to be added to the list, updating the UI automatically.
successCriteria: The addTodo function is defined, takes a text parameter, and calls setTodos to add a new todo with a unique id and the provided text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named addTodo, takes a text parameter, and adds a new todo with a unique id to the todos state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addTodo handler function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named addTodo that adds a new todo to the state with a unique id and the provided text.

steps.title: Add input field and add button
steps.instruction: In your TodoList component's return statement, add an input field and a button. The input should be controlled (its value tied to a new state variable), and the button should call addTodo with the input value when clicked.
steps.hint: Create a new state variable for the input value, add an input element with onChange to update this state, and a button with onClick to call addTodo.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will include an input field for entering new todo text and a button to add it to the list.
successCriteria: A controlled input field is added with its value tied to a state variable and onChange handler.
A button is added with onClick calling addTodo with the input value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input and button, but make sure the input is controlled and the button calls addTodo with the input value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field and add button aren't implemented correctly. Add a controlled input and a button that calls addTodo with the input value.

steps.title: Define toggleTodo and deleteTodo handlers
steps.instruction: Inside your TodoList component, define two functions: toggleTodo (toggles a todo's completed status by adding/removing a completed property) and deleteTodo (removes a todo by its id). Update your todo rendering to include buttons for these actions.
steps.hint: For toggleTodo, use map() to create a new array with the updated todo. For deleteTodo, use filter() to remove the todo with the matching id.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will include toggle and delete buttons for each todo, allowing users to mark todos as completed or remove them from the list.
successCriteria: The toggleTodo function is defined and updates a todo's completed status.
The deleteTodo function is defined and removes a todo by its id.
The rendered todos include buttons for toggling completion and deleting.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent work! You've completed the TodoList component with full CRUD functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined some functions, but make sure both toggleTodo and deleteTodo are implemented correctly and the UI includes buttons for these actions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle and delete functionality is missing or incorrect. Define toggleTodo and deleteTodo handlers and add corresponding buttons to each rendered todo.
